summary.text: Doob's martingale inequality, also known as Kolmogorov's submartingale inequality, is a fundamental result in the study of stochastic processes.
It bounds the probability that a submartingale exceeds a given value over an interval of time.
Informally, the expected value of the process at a final time controls the chance that a sample path reaches above a given value beforehand.

items.prompt: You want to know how likely a fair-game process is to spike above some high level at any point before a final time. What does the inequality use to bound that chance?

options.label: The expected value of the process at the final time
The value at the very first moment only
The number of times the path changes direction
The average of the path over its first half

items.explain: By bounding the running maximum using only its terminal expectation, the inequality lets the final expected value control the chance of reaching above a value beforehand.

items.prompt: The inequality is usually stated for martingales. Which wider class of processes does the core mathematics cover?

options.label: Processes with no randomness
Only processes that never move
Any process whatsoever
Submartingales

items.explain: The result is usually given for martingales, but the core mathematics applies to submartingales.

items.prompt: A martingale has bounded expectations. By bounding extreme excursions of its paths, what does the inequality help show?

options.label: The martingale does not oscillate infinitely
The martingale must stay at its starting value
The martingale must rise forever
The martingale must fall to zero

items.explain: By bounding the probability of extreme excursions, it ensures such martingales do not oscillate infinitely, which supports convergence to a limit.

items.prompt: Compared with many other theorems about stochastic processes, what is notable about the assumptions needed for the proof?

options.label: It needs the process to be very smooth
It needs no restrictive assumptions on the filtration or process
It needs a special filtration chosen with care
It needs the process to take only integer values

items.explain: The proof uses very direct reasoning, so it requires no restrictive assumptions on the filtration or the process itself.

items.prompt: A probability textbook cites Kolmogorov's submartingale inequality. Which result is this the same as?

options.label: The optional stopping theorem
The Black-Scholes formula
Doob's martingale inequality
The Itô isometry

items.explain: Doob's martingale inequality is also known as Kolmogorov's submartingale inequality.

items.prompt: Must the times at which the process is observed form an interval or the natural numbers for the inequality to hold?

options.label: Yes, only whole-number times are allowed
Yes, only a single continuous interval works
Yes, only a finite list of times works
No, it holds for more general index sets

items.explain: The submartingale inequality holds even for more general index sets, which are not required to be intervals or natural numbers.
